28: /// labels is unreadable unless the reader can tell which one is the defect and
29: /// which two are "declared here" and "first used here".
30: pub(all) enum LabelStyle {
31:   Primary
32:   Secondary
33: } derive(Eq, Debug, ToJson)
34: 
35: ///|
36: /// A span of source with an optional note attached.
37: pub(all) struct Label {
38:   source : SourceId
39:   span : Span
40:   style : LabelStyle
41:   /// `None` underlines the span without writing anything beside it, which is
42:   /// what you want when the message above already says everything.
43:   message : String?
44:   /// Tie-break for two labels that would occupy the same underline row: the
45:   /// larger wins the row nearer the source line. Defaults to 0.
46:   priority : Int32
47: } derive(Eq, Debug)

73: /// A machine-applicable repair: replace `span` with `replacement`.
74: ///
75: /// Separate from `Label` because it is not a thing to point at, it is a thing
76: /// to do. A consumer that only renders text shows `description`; a consumer
77: /// wiring up an editor's quick-fix applies the edit and ignores the prose.
78: /// Conflating the two is what forces the second consumer to parse the first
79: /// one's output.
80: pub(all) struct Fix {
81:   source : SourceId
82:   span : Span
83:   replacement : String
84:   description : String
85: } derive(Eq, Debug)
86: 
87: ///|
88: /// One diagnostic: what is wrong, where, and what to do about it.
89: ///
90: /// The fields are the union of what miette, codespan-reporting and ariadne
91: /// each found necessary, and the split between them is the point of this type:
92: /// `message` says what is wrong, `labels` say where, `help` says what to do,
93: /// `notes` say what else to know, and `fixes` say it in a form a machine can
94: /// apply. A consumer that wants none of the rendering can read all five.
95: pub(all) struct Report {
96:   severity : Severity
97:   /// A stable identifier such as `"lang::wrong_indentation"`. Stable is
98:   /// the operative word: it is what a user greps for, what a config file
99:   /// suppresses by, and what a test asserts on -- so it must survive rewording
100:   /// the message, which is exactly why it is not derived from one.
101:   code : String?
102:   message : String
103:   labels : Array[Label]
104:   notes : Array[String]
105:   help : String?
106:   /// Where to read more. Rendered as a trailing link.
107:   url : String?
108:   /// Diagnostics that belong to this one, rendered indented beneath it.
109:   related : Array[Report]
110:   fixes : Array[Fix]
111: }

89: /// Add `file`, `line` and `column` when the source is available.
90: ///
91: /// Silently absent rather than null when it is not: a report about a synthesized
92: /// node has no file, and a consumer checking `has key` reads better than one
93: /// checking `is not null`.
94: fn add_position(
95:   obj : Map[String, Json],
96:   id : @report.SourceId,
97:   span : @report.Span,
98:   cache : &@report.SourceCache,
99: ) -> Unit {
100:   match cache.fetch(id) {
101:     None => ()
102:     Some(src) => {
103:       let (line, col) = src.line_col(span.start)
104:       let (end_line, end_col) = src.line_col(span.end())
105:       obj["file"] = Json::string(src.name)
106:       obj["line"] = Json::number(line.to_double())
107:       obj["column"] = Json::number(col.to_double())
108:       obj["end_line"] = Json::number(end_line.to_double())
109:       obj["end_column"] = Json::number(end_col.to_double())
110:     }
111:   }
112: }
